ARABIC — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.

2. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.

3. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.

4. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.

5. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   C. Only memorise without using the language
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

6. When practising Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening Comprehension.

7. When practising Intensive Reading: Poetry, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Poetry.

8. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.

9. When practising Extensive Reading: Library skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Avoid reading anything related to Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Extensive Reading: Library skills.

10. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.

   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Word class: Verbs and Tenses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Sentence patterns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Speaking Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

5. B — Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening Comprehension.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Poetry.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Extensive Reading: Library skills.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.

12. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word class: Verbs and Tenses; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Sentence patterns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Speaking Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
